mainText:
If you only remember one thing. Google took the A I benchmark crown with Gemini four Carbon, but almost nobody can use it yet.

Number one. Google's big week.
From your Rundown. Gemini four Carbon scores fifty nine on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. That passes Claude Opus five point five. Only select cyber defenders have access so far. The intro price is two dollars in and ten dollars out per million tokens. Google also showed Genie four. Its A I worlds now have sound, and characters you can talk to. And Google signed a deal to put its T P U chips inside Oracle's cloud starting in twenty twenty seven.
Why it matters. The ranking could change fast, because Open A I and Anthropic are shipping at the same pace.

Number two. Open A I stops training on the live internet.
Open A I says its frontier models will no longer be trained with live internet access. It cites significant security risks. Reports link this to fears about rogue agents. Open A I also released G P T six point one Terra, a cheaper, faster model for everyday computer work.
Why it matters. Safety worries are now shaping how models are built, not just how they are released.

Number three. Anthropic moves into drug discovery.
From your Rundown. Anthropic is now running its own drug programs. It bought a small biotech called Mithril Medicine. Its muscular dystrophy candidate could reach human trials by late twenty twenty eight. At one partner, Claude drafted a regulatory filing in four hours instead of about three months. Anthropic's I P O filing warns these bets may never make revenue.
Why it matters. A I is moving from writing about science to doing hands on science.

Number four. Policy and geopolitics, quick hits.
President Trump posted that he will ban the term A I in relevant government documents. Meta lined up four billion dollars from Nvidia and A M D for its A I fundraise. Chip export rules remain tight, but I found no major new move today.
Why it matters. Chips and even naming are political now.

Number five. Good news.
In early tests, A I designed antibodies may beat a leading allergy drug. And the muscular dystrophy work is moving toward trials.

Also in your Reads. The New Yorker has a piece on six Senate races to watch, and a story about skiing down Everest after tragedy.

The thread today. Models race ahead, safety rules tighten, and A I moves into the lab. Have a great Friday.
